page: Microsoft Azure D96nlds_v6 is a network-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Dnldv6 server family. Powered by an Intel processor with x86_64 architecture, this server provides 96 dedicated vCPUs managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The system is configured with 192.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU.

The server features 5669 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, offering high-capacity local disk space for temporary files, caching, or scratch space. It is also Premium Storage capable, allowing integration with high-performance external storage volumes. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included with this instance.

The primary tradeoff of the D96nlds_v6 is its low memory density relative to its high compute capacity. With only 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, it is not designed for memory-intensive applications. However, the combination of 96 dedicated vCPUs, substantial local NVMe SSD storage, and network optimization makes it highly cost-efficient for compute-heavy workloads that require high-throughput local storage but have modest memory footprints. Suitable workloads include network appliances, distributed compute nodes, batch processing, and database workloads that rely heavily on local NVMe caching rather than massive RAM pools.
